account: Today I have followed my appointments: morning office business, a market walk, lunch at home, and town accounts. I have now arrived at the east-bank cottage for three o'clock tea with the neighbour. The unusual item is a vague report of a 'bridge or port change at inn,' which I personally heard from Townsfolk 03 and Townsfolk 23. I asked the secretary to investigate. She reports that the innkeeper made no such proposal or announcement and traced the rumor to Townsfolk 03. The baker told me freight denied seeing any bridge or port change and had only offered delivery help, warehouse space, and ferry service. Builder says the bridge is passable with no confirmed defects, and relayed freight's report of undamaged roads and a trouble-free ferry crossing. Thus I have no confirmed evidence of a route change or any organized activity behind the talk. It may simply be a rumor or a misunderstanding of freight's ordinary business offers; I do not know its purpose. The bakery appears well supplied: I saw the baker stock bread, and he reported seventy-two fresh loaves. He asked about upcoming gatherings, but the secretary said none were listed today or tomorrow. No receipts or expense claims were presented at accounts, and I authorized no repair spending; any specific maintenance need requires a written estimate. My tea entry was imprecise, naming neither host nor exact cottage, but I found the neighbour waiting at the cottage and have asked how things are along the river. I am awaiting an answer. Nothing I have learned yet establishes that anyone is concealing a plan from me.
